name: Wyzant
reason: Started hyper-local in Chicago and hand-onboarded tutors for two years before scaling nationally; acquired by IXL Learning.
description: Two-sided marketplace connecting students with tutors across the US.

name: Preply
reason: Built a programmatic SEO moat with millions of tutor-profile pages before scaling paid acquisition.
description: Global online language tutor marketplace with millions of learners.

name: Varsity Tutors
reason: Pivoted format from 1:1 tutoring to live online classrooms while competitors stayed in old model.
description: Live learning platform (now Nerdy Inc., NYSE: NRDY) for tutoring and classes.

name: Outschool
reason: Owned a narrow vertical (kids' live classes) so completely that incumbents could not enter.
description: Marketplace of live online classes for K-12 learners.

name: Skillshare
reason: Creator-led subscription model with strong content flywheel.
description: Subscription learning platform with creator-produced courses.

name: Duolingo
reason: Free, gamified product drove viral growth and high retention before monetization.
description: Free language-learning app (NASDAQ: DUOL) with hundreds of millions of users.

name: Airbnb
reason: Hand-onboarded the first 1,000 hosts in NYC and shot listing photos personally before scaling.
description: Global marketplace for short-term lodging and experiences.

name: Stripe
reason: Obsessed over developer experience in a category competitors treated as enterprise sales.
description: Payments infrastructure for internet businesses.

name: Notion
reason: Near-bankruptcy rewrite into a flexible block model; rode bottom-up product-led growth.
description: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, and databases.

name: Figma
reason: Bet on browser-based multiplayer when incumbents stayed desktop-only.
description: Collaborative interface design tool used by product teams worldwide.

name: Tutorspree
reason: Could not solve repeat-usage; SEO-driven acquisition collapsed and unit economics never closed.
description: YC-backed marketplace connecting tutors and students.

name: Chegg Tutors
reason: Outcompeted by Wyzant and Varsity Tutors; parent company lost faith in the line.
description: Tutoring service operated as a Chegg product line.

name: Coursmos
reason: Serial pivots, no product-market fit, founder burnout.
description: Microlearning platform for short, on-demand courses.

name: LearnVest Tutors
reason: Negative unit economics on paid acquisition — CAC permanently exceeded LTV.
description: Online tutoring offshoot of the LearnVest finance brand.

name: Quibi
reason: Built a mobile-only short-form product nobody asked for; launched during a pandemic that destroyed commute viewing.
description: Short-form mobile streaming service for premium content.

name: Theranos
reason: Core technology never worked; leadership defrauded investors and patients.
description: Blood-testing startup promising lab results from a single drop.

name: Juicero
reason: $400 connected juicer solved no real problem — packs could be squeezed by hand.
description: Wi-Fi-connected juice press paired with proprietary produce packs.

name: Pets.com
reason: Sold heavy, low-margin goods below cost and burned marketing dollars before logistics existed.
description: Online retailer of pet food and supplies; iconic dot-com bust.

name: WeWork
reason: Long-term lease liabilities funded by short-term memberships; IPO collapse exposed governance failures.
description: Global coworking and flexible-office operator.

name: Webvan
reason: Built billion-dollar warehouse infrastructure before validating demand or unit economics.
description: Online grocery delivery pioneer of the dot-com era.

name: Beepi
reason: Operational overhead and lavish spending outpaced marketplace take rate.
description: Peer-to-peer used-car marketplace.

name: Jawbone
reason: Lost the fitness-tracker race to Fitbit and the smartwatch race to Apple; quality issues eroded trust.
description: Maker of Bluetooth headsets, speakers, and fitness trackers.

name: Friendster
reason: Scaling failures and slow site performance pushed users to MySpace and then Facebook.
description: Early social-networking pioneer that predated Facebook.

name: Shopify
reason: Gave merchants a simple storefront platform and compounded through an app ecosystem and payment rails.
description: Commerce infrastructure platform for online and retail merchants.

name: Instacart
reason: Avoided owning warehouses by using existing retailers and flexible shopper labor before expanding logistics depth.
description: Online grocery marketplace and delivery network.

name: Square
reason: Started with a simple card reader for underserved small merchants, then expanded into a full financial operating system.
description: Payments and financial tools for small businesses.

name: Fast
reason: Spent aggressively before checkout adoption materialized; revenue remained tiny relative to burn.
description: One-click checkout startup for online merchants.

name: Fitbit
reason: Turned step tracking into a mainstream habit before smartwatches absorbed the category; acquired by Google.
description: Consumer fitness trackers and health wearables company.

name: Nest
reason: Made thermostats desirable through premium design, clear energy savings, and smart-home ecosystem pull; acquired by Google.
description: Smart thermostat and connected home device company.

name: Booking.com
reason: Built deep hotel inventory, performance marketing discipline, and conversion optimization into a durable travel marketplace.
description: Global marketplace for hotels, lodging, and travel bookings.

name: Homejoy
reason: High customer acquisition costs, low repeat usage, and worker classification lawsuits undermined the marketplace.
description: On-demand home cleaning marketplace.

name: LinkedIn
reason: Built a high-utility identity graph for professionals before monetizing recruiting and sales workflows.
description: Professional networking platform acquired by Microsoft.

name: Myspace
reason: Product stagnation, spam, and poor performance pushed users to Facebook's cleaner social graph.
description: Early mass-market social network centered on music and personal profiles.

name: Facebook
reason: Started with dense campus networks, expanded identity-based utility, and built a powerful social graph before monetizing ads.
description: Global social networking platform now part of Meta.

name: TripAdvisor
reason: User-generated reviews created durable SEO and trust before travel booking monetization scaled.
description: Travel review and booking platform for hotels, restaurants, and experiences.

name: Stayzilla
reason: Could not scale homestay supply and demand efficiently; cash burn and operational complexity overwhelmed the marketplace.
description: Indian travel and homestay booking marketplace.
